reference: Fixture-backed parity cases branch on Bash's type builtin: candidate executes the dmesg builtin, while system Bash uses GNU awk to parse the documented Linux /dev/kmsg record framing and independently encode the tested output/filter behavior. The deterministic -T case uses GNU coreutils date under UTC. The reference never executes GNU dmesg or reads the host ring buffer, and expected output is never taken from candidate output. Type/help and usage-error checks are documented Bash-builtin contracts. Live kernel operations are deferred.
coverage: Default decoded timestamp output, extension fields, malformed records, and an unterminated final fixture record.
Named multi-facility and multi-level filtering, plus kernel-only filtering.
Deterministic human-readable -T timestamps using a fixed boot epoch and UTC.
Raw priority prefix combined with timestamp suppression.
A record crossing the implementation's 8192-byte read boundary.
Bash type/help metadata and invalid-level usage status.
exclusions: Live /dev/kmsg reading is deferred because it requires an isolated disposable VM with a seeded kernel ring buffer and suitable access.
Console-level changes (-n) and ring-buffer clearing (-c) are deferred because they require CAP_SYSLOG and an isolated disposable VM.
Follow mode with asynchronous live kernel records is not covered.

cases.purpose: Check default timestamp formatting, accepted extension metadata, malformed-header skipping, and output of a final record without a newline against an independent encoder.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,1000000,-;kernel-one
8,2,2000000,-;user-two
2048,3,3000000,-;priority-outside-abi
garbage
8,x,4000000,-;bad-sequence
0,5,4500000,I,subsys=fixture;extended-record
EOF
printf '%s' '16,6,6000000,-;unterminated-final' >> fixture
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg
else
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      header = substr(line, 1, semi - 1)
      message = substr(line, semi + 1)
      n = split(header, fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      priority = fields[1] + 0
      usec = fields[3] + 0
      if (priority > 2047) next
      printf "[%5d.%06d] %s\n", int(usec / 1000000), usec % 1000000, message
    }
  ' fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Compare comma-separated facility and level filters, then kernel-only filtering, against an independent priority-field decoder.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,1,-;kern-emerg
3,2,2,-;kern-err
4,3,3,-;kern-warn
6,4,4,-;kern-info
8,5,5,-;user-emerg
11,6,6,-;user-err
27,7,7,-;daemon-err
29,8,8,-;daemon-notice
EOF
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -f kern,daemon -l warn,err -t
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -k -t
else
  awk -v pass=filtered '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      priority = fields[1] + 0
      if (priority > 2047) next
      facility = int(priority / 8)
      level = priority % 8
      if (pass == "filtered" &&
          !((facility == 0 || facility == 3) && (level == 3 || level == 4))) next
      if (pass == "kernel" && facility != 0) next
      print substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
  awk -v pass=kernel '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      priority = fields[1] + 0
      if (priority > 2047 || int(priority / 8) != 0) next
      print substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Check inclusive --since and --until comparisons at exact microsecond boundaries and exclusion immediately outside them.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,999998,-;before-lower-bound
0,2,999999,-;at-lower-bound
0,3,1000000,-;after-lower-bound
0,4,2000000,-;at-upper-bound
0,5,2000001,-;after-upper-bound
EOF
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -t --since=.999999 --until 2
else
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      usec = fields[3] + 0
      if (usec < 999999 || usec > 2000000) next
      print substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Compare -T wall-clock rendering for fixed record times with an independent GNU date encoder under UTC.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,0,-;boot-start
0,2,1234567,-;one-second-later
EOF
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture BASHDMESG_BOOT_EPOCH=1700000000 dmesg -T
else
  while IFS= read -r record || [[ -n $record ]]; do
    header=${record%%;*}
    message=${record#*;}
    IFS=, read -r priority sequence usec flags rest <<< "$header"
    epoch=$((1700000000 + usec / 1000000))
    stamp=$(date -u -d "@$epoch" '+[%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y] ')
    printf '%s%s\n' "$stamp" "$message"
  done < fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Check the documented raw leading priority field together with -t timestamp suppression.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,1000000,-;kernel raw
11,2,2000000,-;user error
EOF
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -r -t
else
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      priority = fields[1] + 0
      if (priority > 2047) next
      printf "<%d>%s\n", priority, substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Ensure a valid fixture record longer than one 8192-byte read is emitted intact, comparing with an independent line encoder.
cases.script:
printf -v message '%*s' 8200 ''
message=${message// /x}
printf '0,1,1000000,-;%s\n' "$message" > fixture
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -t
else
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      if (fields[1] + 0 > 2047) next
      print substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
fi

cases.purpose: Verify Bash exposes dmesg as a builtin and its help documents the ring-buffer and deterministic fixture interfaces.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]
doc=$(help dmesg)
[[ $doc == *'Read / control the kernel ring buffer via /dev/kmsg.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'--since S'* ]]
printf 'dmesg builtin and help contract available\n'
cases.stdout: dmesg builtin and help contract available

cases.purpose: Check that an invalid level is rejected as a Bash builtin usage error before attempting to open even the relative fixture path.
Read and decode records from the live kernel ring buffer.
cases.reason: Decoder logic executed on regular files only. Live /dev/kmsg reading needs CAP_SYSLOG (dmesg_restrict) and root to seed records; no current driver has either.

cases.purpose: Exercise dmesg -n against the kernel console log level.
cases.reason: No -n invocation executed. The EPERM and usage paths are unprivileged; a successful change needs CAP_SYSLOG and restore of global console level.

cases.purpose: Exercise dmesg -c against a populated kernel ring buffer.
cases.reason: No -c invocation executed. Unprivileged failure and fixture-hook paths are reachable now; live clear needs CAP_SYSLOG plus ring seeding.
